attributes.content:
## Overview

The Run Telemetry card visualizes one software-factory run: where the wall clock and the tokens went, per turn and per ticket, live while the run executes and afterward. It renders entirely from its own attributes — a compact aggregate the factory orchestrator writes and rewrites during a run — and never fetches or parses anything itself.

This is a data instrument, not a document. Numbers carry the page; prose appears only as labels and one-line footnotes.

## Design Language (binding)

- **Surface**: white background (#ffffff). No tinted page background, no dark mode.
- **Typography**: system sans (SF/Inter class). Three text roles only: (1) eyebrow labels — 11px, uppercase, letter-spaced, medium gray; (2) display numbers — large (28-40px), bold, near-black; (3) footnotes/body — 13-14px, medium gray. Long paragraphs are forbidden anywhere on the card.
- **Stat cards**: white, 1px light-gray border (#e5e5e2), 12px radius, generous padding. Inside: eyebrow label, display number, one gray footnote line. The single most important number on the card (model-inference time) renders in accent blue; every other display number is near-black.
- **Color** is reserved for data, never decoration: blue = design/flagship turns, green = build/sonnet turns, pink = review turns, amber = bootstrap, gray = render gate and other machinery. Same hues everywhere a turn type appears (timeline, legend, tables).
- **Tables**: uppercase gray column headers, hairline row rules, no zebra striping, numbers right-aligned with thousands separators, bold only for emphasized rows (subtotals, anomalies).
- **Callout panel**: light gray background, 3px accent-blue left border, one bold lead sentence — used at most once per section.

## Data Shape (the card's fields)

- **run configuration**: brief URL, target realm URL, control realm URL, target phase (design | implementation | hardening | polishing), factory commit, started at, ended at (empty while running), outcome (running | completed | stopped | failed)
- **totals**: wall clock seconds, inference seconds, output tokens, fresh input tokens, cache-read tokens; machinery seconds broken down as validation / render gate / sync (with call count) / startup
- **phases** (containsMany): phase name, wall clock seconds
- **turns** (containsMany): issue id, issue title, turn type (bootstrap | design-foundation | design | build | fix | review | harden), model, effort, started at, duration seconds (empty for the live turn), output tokens, fresh input tokens, cache-read tokens, compacted (boolean)
- **events** (containsMany): timestamp, kind (compaction | skip-phase | seed-hardening | review-bounce | skip-stale-done), detail
- **issues** (containsMany): issue id, title, iteration count, validation steps run, validation passed

## Layout, top to bottom (isolated format)

1. **Header**: eyebrow line "RUN <n> · <TARGET PHASE>", bold title (the run title), one gray subtitle sentence with the key numbers bold inline — e.g. "Four issues, eight agent turns, done in **35:02** with every issue completed." Configuration details (realms, commit, flags) in a single small footnote row.

2. **KPI stat-card row** — four cards:
   - TOTAL: wall clock, footnote = outcome
   - MODEL INFERENCE: inference time in accent blue, footnote = "<n>% of wall clock · <n> turns"
   - EVERYTHING ELSE: machinery time, footnote = "validation <t> · render gate <t> · sync <t> (<n> calls) · startup <t>"
   - COMPACTIONS: count, footnote = "no context-window overflows" when zero, else "<n> × ~17k fresh tokens re-ingested"
   While the run is live, TOTAL ticks client-side from started-at and the outcome footnote reads "running".

3. **Run timeline**: one horizontal track spanning the card. Issue groups labeled above the track with thin rules spanning their turns; each turn is a rounded segment, width proportional to duration, colored by turn type, duration (m:ss) inside the segment when it fits and below it when it does not. Minute axis (0 · 10 · 20 …) below the track. The live turn renders with a pulsing animation, width from elapsed time. Event markers (compaction, review bounce) as thin vertical ticks with tooltips. Legend row of colored squares + "Design turns (flagship)"-style labels underneath.

4. **Per-ticket breakdown** — the "where did the time go" answer, one subsection per issue in run order. Issue title with its total time and share of the run as the subsection header line, then a table of its turns: TURN · MODEL · DURATION · OUTPUT TOKENS · CACHE READ. Bold subtotal row per issue. Footnote row per issue: iteration count and validation outcome; bold the iteration count when above 2. A final TOTAL row across all issues, bold.

5. **Token economics** — the "where did the tokens go" answer, one table like the per-turn cache table: TURN · FRESH INPUT · SERVED FROM CACHE · HIT RATE, with compacted turns bolded (they are the hit-rate outliers). Below it, one callout panel with a computed lead: the turn with the most fresh input, named — e.g. "**SN-1 build re-ingested 17,594 fresh tokens after compaction — ~350× a normal turn.** Cached input is nearly free; fresh input and output are the spend."

6. **Phase subtotals**: one thin horizontal bar per lifecycle phase with seconds and percent of total. Omit phases that did not run.

## Other formats

- **Fitted**: eyebrow (run title) + TOTAL and MODEL INFERENCE numbers + outcome badge. Must read at tile size, white background.
- **Embedded**: header + the four KPI cards + phase subtotal bars.

## Rendering constraints

Plain CSS only: segments and bars are divs with percentage widths, the timeline is flexbox, no charting library, no external assets or fonts. Empty states matter: a card holding only a completed bootstrap turn and one live turn (the first minutes of a run) must render every section sensibly — the per-ticket and token tables show what exists, the phase bars show only phases with time.

## Sample Instances (required)

Create two example instances with realistic data:

1. **A finished run**: 4 issues (bootstrap, design foundation, one feature card, one hardening pass), 7-8 turns, ~35 minutes wall clock, ~90% inference share, a few thousand output tokens, 15-20 million cache-read tokens, tiny fresh-input numbers (double digits) on normal turns and ~17,000 on one compacted build turn, one compaction event, one skip-phase event, one review bounce on the feature issue (3 iterations). Values must look like measurements, not round numbers.
2. **A run in progress**: a completed bootstrap turn and a live design-foundation turn (no duration), outcome running, no ended-at. This instance doubles as the empty-state proof.

## Example Use Cases

- **Live operator view:** the card sits open next to the Run Log while a run executes; the KPI numbers and timeline grow turn by turn and the live turn pulses.
- **Post-run analysis:** a finished run's card answers "where did the time go" per ticket and in total, and "where did the tokens go" per turn, without reading raw trace files.
- **Policy audit:** turn-type coloring makes a mis-budgeted turn (a design turn on the cheap tier, a fix turn on the flagship) visible at a glance.

cardInfo.summary: Data-instrument dashboard for one software-factory run: KPI stat cards, a per-turn timeline, per-ticket time breakdown, and token economics on a white surface.
